clue.text: Possibly time to finish messing about with our crossword, finally — staff should be locked up!

indicators.note: locked up means imprisoned, so the staff go inside the jumbled letters
messing about with something means fiddling with it, so the letters of 'to finish' and 'our' are jumbled
finally points to the closing letter of the word crossword

parts.note: staff are the workers, the men

explanation.surface: An irritated plea: finish fiddling with our crossword, and the staff responsible ought to be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing about' and 'should be locked up' both seem part of the grumble; 'staff' means workers, not a stick. Time is often called the fourth dimension in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is often described in physics as a further dimension beyond length, breadth and height; 'Possibly' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Perhaps two left in a line among manual weapons

indicators.note: among means placed amid, so the short pieces go within the weapons word

parts.note: weapons of the hand are fists

explanation.surface: Two survivors left standing in a row among people armed only with their bare hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is the container signal; 'left' is part of the definition, not the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: When a contest reaches its final, two competitors usually remain; 'Perhaps' signals that two is only one possible number.

clue.text: Release relative, not entirely a killer

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
the asp is a venomous snake, a killer

explanation.surface: A family member set free who was not wholly a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the last letter of UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a clasp is to let go or free something, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Mine triggered by this error message

parts.note: a trip is a slip or mistake
a wire is a telegram, a message

explanation.surface: A computer warning, perhaps, that explodes a mine when it pops up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripwire is a hidden cord that sets off an explosive device when someone catches it with a foot.

clue.text: Philosophy of the puppy feeder?

definitions.meaning: a fixed set of beliefs or doctrine
the mother dog who suckles the pup, read as a dog's ma

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about the outlook of whoever feeds the puppy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as DOG MA: the pup's mum is its feeder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a settled body of doctrine, so it can stand for a philosophy held without question.

clue.text: "Missing" unit — it's taken away, dashed?

indicators.note: dashed means smashed or scattered, so the letters are rearranged
taken away means removed, so 'it' comes out of the word unit

parts.note: the clue's 'it' names the letters to remove, with 's as 'is'

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a unit that has gone missing: has it been carried off in a hurry?
explanation.walkthrough: Removing IT from 'unit' leaves UN; 'dashed' then shuffles MISSING + UN. The whole clue also describes the sign: it means take away, and it is a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: The subtraction symbol tells you a quantity is removed, and it is printed as a short horizontal stroke.

clue.text: Sweet things in book collection most delightful

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the sweets sit inside the book collection

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
ices are frozen desserts, sweet things

explanation.surface: Desserts tucked into a library make the loveliest find.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice means pleasant, so its superlative is the most pleasing or delightful.

clue.text: Repeat, that is, about three times?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the 'that is' letters go round the times

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates 'id est', that is
three words for time: T, ERA and T again

explanation.surface: Saying something again, perhaps a third time over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three times' is three separate words meaning time: T, ERA, T.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to perform or say again, a direct synonym of repeat as a verb.

clue.text: Conductor showing fortitude

definitions.meaning: a fibre carrying signals through the body, a conductor of impulses

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader displaying courage on the podium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra; here it is a body fibre that conducts impulses.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve carries electrical impulses, and nerve also means boldness or steadiness under pressure.

clue.text: Being amorous in the centre of Birmingham with Elvis?

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre, by Birmingham
Elvis Presley was called the King of rock and roll

explanation.surface: A rock star turning romantic in a big English city's centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of Birmingham' tempts you to take the middle letters; it is the NEC, the National Exhibition Centre, a large venue near Birmingham, the UK city.
explanation.definitionFit: Necking is informal for kissing and cuddling, so it means behaving amorously.

clue.text: Modern sound then obvious, basic to the core?

indicators.note: sound signals that the word for modern is replaced by a word heard the same way

parts.note: modern means new
clear means obvious

explanation.surface: Something up to date, then plain, and fundamental right through.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear means relating to a nucleus, the central core, and so is fundamental to it.

clue.text: Field bound to be cut

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter of the word for bound goes

parts.note: a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A meadow that is certain to be mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be cut' reads as 'sure to be mown', but 'bound' is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for a meadow or grassland, a field.

clue.text: The man I saw's recollected? No!

definitions.text: The man I saw's recollected? No!

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered up again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trying to recall the man I saw, and failing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' here, so its S counts. Read whole, the clue is someone who cannot remember a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is what people say when they cannot remember someone's name, fitting a failed recollection.

clue.text: Inspector cunningly concealing university second degree in music

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the jumbled letters hold the university letter
cunningly means craftily, so the word's letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A sly police inspector hiding his university master's degree in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second degree' suggests an academic qualification; it is the second note of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In a major or minor scale the note one step above the tonic is named for that position, the scale's second degree.

clue.text: Diversity there on abandoned ship

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the letters run loose

parts.note: SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: Variety found on a deserted vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned ship' looks like one phrase; 'abandoned' acts on 'there on', and 'ship' is SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherness is the quality of being different or distinct, close in sense to diversity.

clue.text: Inventor of the phone call?

definitions.meaning: Alexander Graham, credited with the telephone
in British slang, give someone a ring on the phone

explanation.surface: Who invented the telephone call?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give me a bell' is British slang for 'phone me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone, and a phone call is informally a ring of that name.

clue.text: Giant in dispute with neighbour idly playing with alien

indicators.note: playing with means toying with, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A huge figure quarrelling next door, lazily toying with a visitor from space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant' suggests an ogre; it is a fast-growing conifer, whose tall hedges cause boundary rows between neighbours in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This cypress hybrid grows enormously fast and is notorious in British suburbs for hedge disputes between neighbours.

clue.text: Glass tubes broken up for starters, one of us getting knocked over

indicators.note: starters are the first letters, here of broken and up
knocked over means upended, which in a down clue turns the word upside down

parts.note: the setter is one of the crossword compilers speaking here

explanation.surface: Laboratory glassware smashed, and a colleague bowled over in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting knocked over' reverses SETTER into RETTES.
explanation.definitionFit: A burette is a graduated glass tube with a tap, used in chemistry to measure liquid.

clue.text: See 20
Is a route across the Channel going north of a huge land mass?

indicators.note: going north means climbing, so in a down clue the pieces read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
rue is French for street, a route on the other side of the Channel

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a cross-Channel route heading north reaches a vast continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'route across the Channel' suggests the tunnel; it is the French word RUE. Going north turns IS A + RUE into EURASI, which sits 'north of' (above) A.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe and Asia together form one continuous continent, the largest land mass on Earth.

clue.text: Anything misbehaving types put on as a consequence? That's it!

definitions.text: Anything misbehaving types put on as a consequence? That's it!

indicators.note: put on means added after, so the jumbled types follow the other pieces

parts.note: then means as a result
aught is an old word for anything

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting up, so the letters are disorderly

explanation.surface: A parent's punishment for misbehaving children: is that it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges TYPES into YSTEP. Read whole, the clue describes where naughty children are put as a consequence, a technique popularised by TV's Supernanny.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair or spot where a misbehaving child must sit for a while, as a timeout punishment.

clue.text: Japanese cooker hot with vital energy, one degree higher

indicators.note: higher means above, which in a down clue puts these pieces before the life force

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree
chi is the life force in Chinese thought

explanation.surface: A Japanese stove: hot, with life force, and turned up a notch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'higher' places I + BA above CHI in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hibachi is a small charcoal brazier used in Japan for heating and grilling food.

clue.text: Smart clothes are endlessly turning up for French politician

indicators.note: clothes means covers, so the smart word wraps round the rest

parts.note: chic means stylish, smart

indicators.note: turning up means flipping upwards, which in a down clue reverses the letters
endlessly means without the last letter

explanation.surface: Smart outfits keep coming into fashion for a Paris statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb meaning covers, not garments; 'endlessly' trims and 'turning up' reverses, as it does in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Chirac served as President of France and as its Prime Minister.

clue.text: Spanner beginning to rotate, accessing both nuts in kitchen appliance

indicators.note: accessing means getting into, so the jumbled letters enter the appliance

parts.note: a fridge is a kitchen appliance

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go haywire
beginning to means the first letter of the word rotate

explanation.surface: A spanner starts turning, reaching both nuts inside a kitchen appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanner' looks like a wrench but means something that spans; 'nuts' is the anagram signal rather than hardware, and 'accessing' puts the jumble inside the appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forth Bridge is the famous Scottish railway bridge spanning the Firth of Forth, so a spanner in the literal sense.

clue.text: Slip down

explanation.walkthrough: Fluff can be a verb, to bungle, and a noun for soft fuzz.
explanation.definitionFit: To fumble a line is to make a slip, and soft fine feathers or fibres are fuzz.

clue.text: King getting wings clipped over female, very petite

indicators.note: over means above, so in a down clue the trimmed king sits on top
clipped wings means both outer letters of the king's name are cut off

parts.note: Edward is a name borne by several English kings

explanation.surface: A king, his wings trimmed, standing over a tiny woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting wings clipped' strips the ends of EDWARD to leave DWAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarf can be an adjective for something unusually small, as in dwarf conifers.

clue.text: Intelligence lacking in underwear

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the word in is taken out

parts.note: brain means intelligence, as in 'has a brain'

explanation.surface: A lack of intelligence shown in someone's choice of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is women's supporting undergarment, and its short form is everyday.

clue.text: Delivery service longing for improvement

parts.note: UPS is the parcel carrier United Parcel Service
an urge is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A courier company yearning to do better.
explanation.definitionFit: An upsurge is a sudden increase or rise, a kind of upturn or betterment.

clue.text: A racket involving queen, say, backfiring — so stomach calmer?

indicators.note: backfiring means going backwards, so the letters run the other way
involving means taking in, so the noise wraps around the animal

parts.note: din means a loud noise, a racket
a queen is a female cat, one example

explanation.surface: A noisy scheme with a royal backfires, needing something to settle the nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen, say' looks royal; a queen is a female cat. 'backfiring' turns DCATIN round to NTACID.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid neutralises stomach acid and so settles indigestion, calming the stomach.

clue.text: Old money is securing items of furniture — is one for an Italian friar?

parts.note: the franc is the former currency of France

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the first 'is' surrounds the furniture

parts.note: taken as written
sofas are pieces of furniture
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Old cash locked up around furniture; is one of them suited to an Italian monk?
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of the Franciscan order was a thirteenth-century friar from Assisi, in Umbria.
